title: The Tiger, the Brahmin, and the Jackal
summary: A tiger trapped in a cage tricks a brahmin into freeing him, then threatens to eat him. A clever jackal saves the brahmin by tricking the tiger back into the cage.
moral: Cunning can save you from even the most dangerous situations

acts.name: betrayal
acts.summary: Freed tiger wants to eat brahmin

acts.name: rescue
acts.summary: Jackal tricks tiger back into cage

title: The Four Friends
summary: A deer, mouse, crow, and tortoise form a friendship pact and save each other from hunters.
moral: True friendship is the greatest treasure

acts.name: rescue
acts.summary: Friends combine skills to free deer

title: The Singing Donkey
summary: A donkey sings loudly in a field at night and is beaten by the angry farmer whose crops he was eating.
moral: There is a time and place for everything

acts.name: feast
acts.summary: Donkey and jackal eat crops at night

title: The Bird and the Monkeys
summary: A bird advises shivering monkeys to build a shelter; they destroy the bird's nest in anger.
moral: Do not give advice to those who will not appreciate it

title: The Cat Who Served the Lion
summary: A cat serves a lion faithfully but grows arrogant; when challenged by a dog, the cat's true cowardly nature emerges.
moral: Borrowed power does not change your true nature

acts.name: exposure
acts.summary: Dog chases cat up a tree

title: The Merchant's Son
summary: A lazy merchant's son squanders his father's fortune, learns the value of hard work through poverty.
moral: Wealth without wisdom is quickly lost

acts.name: lesson
acts.summary: Sage teaches him the value of labor

title: The Mice and the Cat
summary: Mice tie a bell on a sleeping old cat; when the cat awakes, mice can hear it coming.
moral: Clever planning can neutralize even feared enemies

acts.name: fear
acts.summary: Mice live in terror of cat

acts.name: plan
acts.summary: Brave mouse ties bell on sleeping cat

title: The Jackal and the Dead Elephant
summary: A jackal finds a dead elephant but cannot pierce the tough hide. Through patience and trickery, he gets a lion to open it for him.
moral: Patience and cunning achieve what brute force alone cannot

title: The Dove and the Bee
summary: A dove saves a drowning bee; later the bee stings a hunter about to shoot the dove.
moral: Every act of kindness finds its way back to you

acts.name: rescue
acts.summary: Dove drops a leaf for drowning bee

title: The Lion and the Old Hare
summary: An old hare tricks a greedy lion into fighting his own reflection in a well.
moral: Even the mighty fall to their own arrogance

acts.name: defeat
acts.summary: Lion attacks own reflection in well

title: The Crane and the Snake
summary: A crane invites a snake to eat the fish who mock him; the snake eats the fish and then the crane.
moral: Inviting your enemy to solve your problems creates a bigger problem

acts.name: alliance
acts.summary: Crane invites snake to eat fish

title: The Golden Swan
summary: A swan with golden feathers gives one feather at a time to a poor woman; she plucks all at once and they turn white.
moral: Greed destroys the gift of generosity

title: The Elephants and the King of Mice
summary: Elephant herd tramples mouse village; mouse king negotiates and later mice free trapped elephants.
moral: Even the smallest ally can save you in time of need

title: The Monkey and the Cap Seller
summary: A cap seller sleeps under a tree; monkeys take his caps. He throws his own cap down and monkeys imitate him.
moral: Clever observation of behavior can solve problems

title: The Tortoise and the Swan
summary: Two swans carry a tortoise by a stick, but the tortoise talks and falls to his death.
moral: Know when to keep your mouth shut

acts.name: plan
acts.summary: Swans agree to fly tortoise to new pond

title: The Farmer and the Stork
summary: A stork caught among cranes being netted pleads innocence; the farmer judges by company kept.
moral: You are judged by the company you keep

title: The Talkative Turtle
summary: A turtle ignores friends' advice to stay silent during flight and falls when he argues with passersby.
moral: Pride in one's opinions can be self-destructive

acts.name: agreement
acts.summary: Turtle must stay silent during flight

title: The Blue Bull
summary: A jackal paints himself blue and rules the forest as a divine being until he instinctively howls.
moral: You cannot suppress your true nature forever

title: The Wise Minister
summary: A minister solves the king's impossible riddles by observing nature and applying folk wisdom.
moral: Observation and folk wisdom often surpass book learning

title: The Loyal Dog
summary: A dog guards his master's home against thieves even when offered meat to stay quiet.
moral: True loyalty cannot be bought

acts.name: temptation
acts.summary: Thief offers dog meat to be quiet

acts.name: loyalty
acts.summary: Dog barks louder and alerts master
